summary: Invoice tokens higher than Console usage by ~6% (Hosted API) — suspected retry double-counting
description:
Customer reported that Feb invoice token totals are ~6% higher than Console usage page for the same period.

Account / Contract:
- Customer: Northwind Analytics (Enterprise Hosted API)
- Billing period in question: 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-31 (invoice issued 2026-02-02)
- Invoice line items involved: Hosted API - Input Tokens, Hosted API - Output Tokens
- Customer reference: “Console shows 1.94B tokens for January; invoice totals 2.06B tokens (~6% higher).”

Impact:
- Amount at risk: customer indicated they will dispute/hold payment if delta not explained or corrected.
- Risk: trust issue + potential precedent for other accounts if systemic.

Initial hypothesis (from triage):
- Console and invoice aggregation may differ due to (a) time zone windowing, (b) model alias mapping, (c) rounding policy differences, (d) retries / request replays being counted as billable in one pipeline but deduped in another.

Customer-facing ask:
- Provide root cause, verify whether overbilled, and confirm remediation (credit/refund) and prevention.

Support checklist artifacts requested from customer:
- Invoice PDF + line item detail
- Console screenshot/export for the same time range
- Approximate endpoints used (chat/completions/embeddings), top models, and whether streaming enabled

Internal artifacts pulled:
- Billing export invoice_run_id: inv_2026_02_02_0131Z (Finance)
- Console usage export (internal admin): usage_export_northwind_2026-01
- Query: compare raw_telemetry_agg vs billing_ready_agg by day + endpoint + model + region

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on token mismatch (not price changes). Customer did not report abnormal request volume, only mismatch between views.

Next steps:
1) Reconcile invoice totals vs telemetry aggregates by day and endpoint.
2) Confirm whether retry tokens were double-counted as billable tokens in billing pipeline.
3) If confirmed, quantify overbilled units, initiate credit approval, and coordinate backfill (if applicable).
comments: 2026-02-05 09:14 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Customer (Northwind) reports invoice tokens higher than Console by ~6% for Jan. Requested invoice + console export; starting internal reconciliation. Looping in Finance (Emily) and Telemetry (Logan/Nadia).

2026-02-05 10:02 PT — Emily Stone (Billing Controls): Pulled invoice_run_id inv_2026_02_02_0131Z and billing export totals. Invoice shows: Input 1,244,992,180 tokens; Output 813,771,044 tokens; Total 2,058,763,224. Console export shared by Support shows Total 1,944,xxx,xxx (needs exact). Delta ~114M tokens. This is too large to be rounding-only; likely retries or windowing.

2026-02-05 10:41 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry): Ran quick diff by day. Delta concentrated on 2026-01-17 through 2026-01-20, mostly chat/completions, region us-east, models rw-chat-v3 + llama-3-70b-instruct. Not seeing missing days. Suggest looking at request_id duplication / retry behavior around those dates (we had a transient 5xx spike in us-east).

2026-02-05 11:23 PT — Allison Grant (Observability): Confirmed elevated 5xx + upstream timeouts in us-east API gateway 2026-01-18 02:00–05:00 UTC. Customers likely retried. If pipeline counts both initial attempt + retry as separate billable tokens without outcome filtering, would explain ~5–7% increase for that window.

2026-02-06 08:17 PT — Nadia Rahman (Metering Pipelines): Found inconsistency: Console usage de-dupes by canonical request_id (prefers final successful attempt) and suppresses tokens for attempts marked as retried; billing_ready_agg currently cannot distinguish retry attempts vs terminal attempts because metering events do not include request_outcome/retry_reason dimension in the aggregation table. Net effect: billing_ready_agg sums tokens across all attempts, including internal retries after transient failures.

Example (sanitized):
- request_id: req_01HNY... had attempt_id a1 (timeout) then a2 (success). Telemetry has two token events. Console shows only a2; billing sums a1+a2.

This matches ENG-4823 scope (add retry dimensions) and should be fixable with backfill + filter rule to bill only terminal outcomes.

2026-02-06 09:05 PT — Emily Stone (Billing Controls): If we confirm overbilling, we should issue credit rather than revise already-issued invoice (preferred). Need quantified number of overbilled tokens and $ amount, plus sign-off per runbook. Please provide breakdown and proposed remediation to share with customer.

2026-02-06 12:38 PT — Logan Wright (Telemetry): Quantification for Northwind Jan period:
- Overcount attributable to duplicate retry attempts: 112,846,390 tokens (input 68,210,774; output 44,635,616)
- Concentrated on 2026-01-18 and 2026-01-19 during us-east gateway instability
- Estimated $ impact (per contracted token rates): $3,942.73

Method: joined billing token events to request attempt table, selected attempt_rank > 1 as retry duplicates, summed tokens; cross-checked against console export which already suppresses those duplicates. Confidence high (matches delta within 1.1%).

2026-02-07 09:12 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Draft customer explanation:
- Console displays billable tokens from final/terminal request attempt; invoice pipeline included tokens from transient failed attempts that were retried.
- Issue limited to a short window correlated with elevated gateway errors.
- We will credit the difference and prevent recurrence by updating metering pipeline to classify outcomes and filter non-billable retry attempts.

Emily/Legal: please confirm wording acceptable (avoid implying systemic misbilling beyond this period).

2026-02-07 10:20 PT — Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel): Wording OK as long as we avoid “incorrectly billed across all customers.” Suggest: “In this billing period, a subset of retried attempts were included in the invoice aggregation; we have identified and corrected the issue for your account and are rolling out a general fix.” Also state the dispute/credit is “one-time adjustment for this invoice.”

2026-02-08 14:06 PT — Emily Stone (Billing Controls): Approved one-time credit for $3,942.73 against invoice inv_2026_02_02_0131Z, pending CFO approval threshold check (under delegated limit). Will apply as credit memo on next invoice unless customer requests immediate adjustment. Dev: confirm customer preference.

2026-02-09 09:31 PT — Dev Patel (Support): Customer prefers credit memo applied to next invoice (no re-issue needed). Sent explanation + credit confirmation. Customer asked whether Feb usage is impacted; told them fix is being rolled out and we’ll monitor their account.

2026-02-10 16:22 PT — Nadia Rahman (Metering Pipelines): Engineering update: PR github/redwood/pr_41917 adds request_outcome + retry_reason to metering events and downstream aggregates with cardinality safeguards. Backfill plan in ENG-4826 to regenerate billing aggregates for targeted Jan window and validate no invoice deltas beyond tolerance. Note: this does not change already-issued invoices; used for monitoring + preventing recurrence.

2026-02-12 11:08 PT — Emily Stone (Billing Controls): Credit memo created and recorded in billing system; attached to account. Added Northwind to enhanced monitoring list until daily reconciliation job is live (PR 41872). Marking ticket resolved.
resolution: Root cause: Billing aggregation included tokens from transient failed request attempts that were retried (retry attempts lacked outcome metadata in billing_ready_agg), while Console de-duplicated to terminal/successful attempts. Quantified overcount for Jan: 112,846,390 tokens (~$3,942.73). Remediation: issued one-time credit memo to apply to next invoice; engineering fix in progress to add request_outcome/retry_reason dimensions and enable filtering + reconciliation (PR 41917) plus ongoing daily reconciliation monitoring (PR 41872).
